nodes.name: TST_Mineral_Kinetics
nodes.description: Transition-state-theory rate law. The volumetric rate is -(reactive surface area) x (affinity factor) x (rate constant), in mol/sec per m^3 bulk [src: reaction_mineral.F90:1274-1281]. TWO DISTINCT RATE ROUTINES EXIST and the deck selects between them implicitly -- see the AFFINITY_THRESHOLD entry.

nodes.name: Reactive_Surface_Area_Evolution
nodes.description: Specific surface area evolves with porosity and/or mineral volume fraction through SURFACE_AREA_FUNCTION. The porosity factor uses the SOLID fraction, ((1-phi_base)/(1-phi_0))**power [src: reaction_mineral.F90:2052-2055], so its sign of effect is opposite to the naive reading of its name.

nodes.name: Porosity_Permeability_Feedback
nodes.description: Mineral volume change updates porosity absolutely [src: realization_subsurface.F90:2226-2227], and porosity then rescales permeability through a thresholded power law with a LOWER clamp [src: realization_subsurface.F90:2062-2070]. The source contains NO kozeny or carman string, so naming it Kozeny-Carman would be an invention.

nodes.name: Van_Genuchten_WRM
nodes.description: Capillary-pressure/saturation relation. Pc = (Se**(-1/m) - 1)**(1/n) / alpha, with n = 1/(1-m) DERIVED from m and Se = (Sl - Sr)/(1 - Sr) [src: characteristic_curves_common.F90:860-867]. At or below Sr the capillary pressure is clamped to pcmax [src: characteristic_curves_common.F90:852-854].

nodes.name: Mualem_Relative_Permeability
nodes.description: Relative permeability of liquid and gas derived from the retention curve. The liquid and gas forms take SEPARATE parameter copies -- in this deck MUALEM_VG_LIQ and MUALEM_VG_GAS each carry their own M and LIQUID_RESIDUAL_SATURATION [deck: pflotran.in:574-583].
nodes.code_location: characteristic_curves_common.F90:148-157 (liq type), :159-165 (gas type), :3366-3417 (gas rel-perm, formula at :3409); deck addresses at pflotran.in:574-583

nodes.name: GIRT_Reactive_Transport
nodes.description: Global-implicit reactive transport -- chemistry and transport solved together, as opposed to operator-split OSRT. Selected in this deck [deck: pflotran.in:19].

nodes.name: Advection_Dispersion_Diffusion
nodes.description: Solute flux from Darcy advection, mechanical dispersion and molecular diffusion. With USE_MILLINGTON_QUIRK_TORTUOSITY the diffusion coefficient is scaled by saturation**(7/3) * porosity**(1/3) [src: transport.F90:113-114, :157-165]. That option additionally REQUIRES every TORTUOSITY to remain at its default of 1 [src: pm_rt.F90:469-483].

nodes.name: Seepage_Face_Boundary
nodes.description: NOT EAST-ONLY: the same FLOW_CONDITION `gas_vent` (hence the same DIRICHLET_SEEPAGE type) is coupled to the east seepage face [deck: pflotran.in:535-539] AND to the top surface as `top_vent` [deck: pflotran.in:528-532]. The `#skip`/`#noskip` around the latter are plain COMMENTS, not directives -- a line beginning with `#` is discarded before the SKIP test [src: input_aux.F90:797, :811] -- so `top_vent` is live, which its 62 output columns confirm. The east face is the drainage boundary [deck: pflotran.in:473; src: condition.F90:1323-1324, pflotran_constants.F90:222 DIRICHLET_SEEPAGE_BC = 30]. The one-way clamp is armed by the BC TYPE, not by any saturation value. Of the FIVE bc_types that reach this Darcy-flux branch at all [src: general_common.F90:2653-2654 -- DIRICHLET, HYDROSTATIC, HYDROSTATIC_SEEPAGE, HYDROSTATIC_CONDUCTANCE, DIRICHLET_SEEPAGE], the three seepage/conductance types fall into the `case default` that sets `water_cannot_flow_in` when capillary pressure is positive [src: general_common.F90:2677-2684]; DIRICHLET and HYDROSTATIC do not. Other bc_types (NEUMANN_BC at [src: general_common.F90:2780]) never enter this branch -- so "every bc_type other than ..." would be a false universal. THE CLAMP ITSELF is a few lines further on and is explicitly gated on the type: `if (bc_type == DIRICHLET_SEEPAGE_BC) then / if (delta_pressure > 0 .and. water_cannot_flow_in) delta_pressure = 0` [src: general_common.F90:2726-2728].

nodes.name: Aqueous_Speciation
nodes.description: Equilibrium speciation of the 16 primary components into 104 secondary species [deck: pflotran.in:93-197 -- 105 lines, of which :110 `!MgNO3+` is commented out], setting the ion activity products the rate law compares against. Constraint TYPE letters are read at [src: transport_constraint_rt.F90:306-345]; types M / G / SC additionally REQUIRE a 4th column naming the constraining phase [src: transport_constraint_rt.F90:348-358].

nodes.name: Timestep_Control
nodes.description: Timestep sizing and cutting. DIAGNOSTIC, never calibration. MAX_TS_CUTS is a PER-TIMESTEP CONSECUTIVE budget -- the counter resets at the top of every timestep [src: timestepper_SNES.F90:371] and the field is documented as "Maximum number of timestep cuts within one time step" [src: timestepper_base.F90:32]. The `cuts` figure in an end-of-run summary is a LIFETIME total and is UNRELATED to this limit. A genuine exhaustion aborts with exit status 88 [src: timestepper_base.F90:740-746; pflotran_constants.F90:63 EXIT_FAILURE = 88] and writes a `<pmname>_cut_to_failure` snapshot [src: timestepper_base.F90:764].

nodes.name: PERM_ISO
nodes.description:

[deck: pflotran.in:554]. Anisotropic alternatives (PERM_X/Y/Z) exist but

PERM_ISO x scale, where scale is the thresholded porosity power law
[src: realization_subsurface.F90:2062-2070].

nodes.name: PERMEABILITY_POWER
nodes.description:
Exponent in the porosity-permeability power law. 3.0 in this deck
[deck: pflotran.in:559]. The relation is
scale = ((phi_base - phi_crit) / (phi_0 - phi_crit)) ** power,
evaluated only when BOTH porosities exceed phi_crit, and otherwise zero
[src: realization_subsurface.F90:2061-2067].

The source contains NO kozeny or carman string -- calling this
Kozeny-Carman would be an invention.
